newsitem.title: TURKEY: Turkish automotive output rises 16 pct in March.
newsitem.headline: Turkish automotive output rises 16 pct in March.

text.p: Turkey's motor vehicle output was 32,190 units in March, up 16 percent from March 1996, while it rose five percent to 76,665 units in the first quarter, from the same period in 1996.

The automotive industry association (OSD) said the leading car output rose six percent to 19,634 units in March, but fell six percent to 46,769 units in the January-March period, compared to a year ago.

First quarter output included 1,783 midibuses, up 118 percent from the same 1996 period, 8,859 trucks, up 86 percent, 5,408 pick-ups, up 49 percent, 790 buses, up 42 percent, and 2,379 minibuses, up 25 percent.
Tractor output dropped six percent to 10,610 in the first quarter, the OSD said.

Car sales in January-March jumped 29.2 percent from the same 1996 period to 53,555 units, mainly due to a sharp increase in imported car sales. The share of imports in total car sales leapt to 29 percent from previous 17.4 percent.
Domestic car sales increased 11.2 percent in January-March, while imported car sales jumped 115.3 percent when compared with the first quarter of 1996.
The OSD statement said automotive and parts industry exports fell 19 percent in the first three months of 1997.
